INFP>ESTJ.yure_s: All four are different, so your whole result can change with the scene. Decide first whether you're picturing yourself running a student council meeting or watching a movie alone on your day off, and your answers will settle down.
INFP>ESTJ.plus: You wonder if you were too strict because you notice how people feel. Someone who keeps things on track and understands people is a huge help on any team.
INFP>ESTJ.tip: On days you're running things, take one minute at the end to tell each person, "This part really helped." It lifts their mood, and yours too.
INFP>ESTJ.hidden: You organize people smoothly, but you were also born good at imagining what doesn't exist yet. While making slides, don't you sometimes think, "If I show it this way, it'll land better"? Try sharing those ideas, and everyone will feel more motivated too.
INFP>ESTJ.hidden_s: You organize people smoothly, but you were also born good at imagining what doesn't exist yet. While making slides for a presentation, don't you sometimes think, "If I show it this way, it'll land better"? Try sharing those ideas, and everyone will feel more motivated too.

INFP>ESFJ.title: Someone who likes doing things for others.
INFP>ESFJ.body: You prepare carefully for a welcome party at work and even get a present for the newcomer. On the day, you notice who's drinking what and offer to order before their glass is empty. You love doing things for people, but you also need time to zone out alone.
INFP>ESFJ.body_s: You prepare carefully for your club's welcome party for new members and even get presents for the new younger members. On the day, you watch for anyone who hasn't joined the conversation and go sit right next to them to talk. You love doing things for people, but you also need time to zone out alone.
INFP>ESFJ.say: "I already booked the place! The rest is a surprise."
INFP>ESFJ.do: For a friend's housewarming, you go through several shops to pick something that fits their room.
INFP>ESFJ.do_s: For a friend's birthday, you go through several shops to pick something that fits their room.
INFP>ESFJ.worry: The more you try to meet everyone's expectations, the less time you get to zone out alone. Going along with everyone, you start to feel that wanting your own things is selfish.
INFP>ESFJ.karai: Even with a drama's villain, you think, "Maybe they have their reasons."
INFP>ESFJ.aru: At get-togethers with friends, you plan the seats and food and even set up a surprise. After everyone leaves, you sit on the couch and zone out for a while.
INFP>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who recharges by resting alone, imagines new things, and moves wherever your mood takes you. Through dealing with all kinds of people, you became able to move among others and prepare properly based on past experience. Wanting to make people happy has been the same since way back. Throughout the get-together you're looking out for how everyone is doing, so when everyone has gone home and you're alone, you can finally relax and want to zone out for a while.
INFP>ESFJ.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change each time. Picture yourself doing things for others or picture yourself daydreaming alone, and a different type may come up.
INFP>ESFJ.plus: You worry about being selfish because you care about the people around you. Because you have time alone to rest, you can go back to doing things for people.
INFP>ESFJ.tip: Keep the day after a get-together free of plans. Resting alone clears your tiredness, so you can enjoy getting ready for the next one too.
INFP>ESFJ.hidden: You like to prepare well, but you were also born able to move freely in the moment. On a day things didn't go as planned, haven't you laughed and said, "Okay, let's do this instead"? Use that, and you'll feel it's fine even if your prep isn't perfect.

INFP>ISTP.title: You quietly make things with your hands.
INFP>ISTP.body: You fix old furniture yourself and repaint it in a color you like while you're at it. For parts you don't know how to do, you watch videos and try a few times until you find a way that works. You're better at working with your hands than putting your feelings into words.
INFP>ISTP.say: "No plans today. Might go out if I feel like it."
INFP>ISTP.do: On your day off, you head out for a walk alone without picking a place.
INFP>ISTP.worry: You're not good at putting feelings into words, so your kindness can look curt. Even when logic says it's fine, your hands stop if your heart isn't on board.
INFP>ISTP.karai: Once you start a game alone, you can't stop, and suddenly it's the middle of the night.
INFP>ISTP.aru: You quietly fixed a friend's bike, but when they say "Thanks," all you can say is "No big deal." You're actually really happy.
INFP>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type who imagines new things and decides with your feelings. As you gained experience, you became able to look at what's in front of you, work with your hands, and figure out how to fix things with logic. Caring about people is still as it was when you were born. Even when you're happy they're pleased, you're not used to putting that feeling into words, so when someone says "Thanks," you get shy and can only say, "No big deal."
INFP>ISTP.yure: The two differences are hunches or facts, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself making something or picture yourself lost in a work you love, and your result can change.
INFP>ISTP.plus: You say "No big deal" because you care so much it's embarrassing. Your quiet help really does reach people.
INFP>ISTP.tip: When words are hard, just add "But I'm glad" after "No big deal." On days you can't even say that, a smile and a nod are fine.
INFP>ISTP.hidden: You're good at working with what's in front of you, but you were born good at imagining what doesn't exist yet. While gazing outside, don't stories or pictures sometimes spread out in your head? Use that, and you can make something that's all your own.

INFP>ISFP.title: When the sky looks pretty, you can't help taking a photo.
INFP>ISFP.body: You keep stones and leaves you picked up on trips lined up in a small box. For the little things in your room, you choose only ones whose color or feel you love. You also like zoning out and imagining all kinds of things.
INFP>ISFP.say: "I kind of like this shop. Can we pop in for a sec?"
INFP>ISFP.do: On a nice day, you change your plans and relax on a park bench.
INFP>ISFP.worry: You have so many things you love, but you don't know how to connect them to your future. You don't like clashing with people, so you tend to swallow what you want to say.
INFP>ISFP.karai: "I love them all, I can't choose," you say, and buy the same top in two colors.
INFP>ISFP.aru: Your phone is full of photos of food and flowers. Every time you look back, you remember "I felt like this that day," and you can't delete any of them.
INFP>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type who imagines new things and what they mean. As the years went by, you came to enjoy the colors and textures right in front of you. Valuing feelings has been the same since way back. Each photo holds the exact mood you felt at the time, so every time you look back, that day comes back to you, and you can't delete any of them.
INFP>ISFP.yure: The only difference is hunches or facts and experience. Picture your everyday life and you lean toward experience. Picture your future dreams and you lean toward hunches.
INFP>ISFP.plus: You notice flowers by the road because you look closely at what's around you. You're good at enjoying everyday life.
INFP>ISFP.tip: Pick your three favorite photos from all you've taken and line them up. You'll see the colors and moods they share, and it'll be easier to say what you like.
INFP>ISFP.hidden: You're good at enjoying everyday life, but you were also born good at imagining what's ahead. Don't you sometimes wonder, "Where would I like to be living in five years?" Use that, and you'll start to see how to connect what you love to your future.

INFP>ESTP.title: When a friend is unsure, you're the one saying "Let's go!"
INFP>ESTP.body: On trips, you're quick to head into places that aren't in the guidebook: "Let's try it." But afterward you worry, "Did everyone have fun?" If a sport catches your interest, you find a trial session and sign up for that weekend. You're active when you're out, but quiet time alone to think matters to you too.
INFP>ESTP.say: "Let's just go and figure it out there. It'll probably work out."
INFP>ESTP.do: When you go clothes shopping, you end up trying on a color you never wear.
INFP>ESTP.worry: After acting on impulse, you're alone thinking, "Did anyone feel bad?" People tend to see you as up for anything, so it's hard to say when you want a quiet day.
INFP>ESTP.karai: "Just a quick trip to the convenience store" takes 30 minutes.
INFP>ESTP.aru: You talk a friend into their first bouldering session, "It'll be fun!", and you're the one who gets hooked. On the train home your friend is quiet, and you start to wonder, "Did I push them into it?"
INFP>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type who recharges by resting alone, imagines new things, and decides with your feelings. Through dealing with all kinds of people, you started getting energy among others too and became able to throw yourself fully into what's in front of you. Worrying about the other person's feelings is still there, just as it was when you were born. While you're playing, you're absorbed in having fun yourself, but when you see your friend quiet on the train home, you suddenly worry about how they feel.
INFP>ESTP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Take it after a day out and about, or after a day thinking alone, and a different type may come up.
INFP>ESTP.plus: You worry you pushed too hard because you really wanted your friend to have fun. You invite people and check on them afterward, so your friends feel at ease.
INFP>ESTP.tip: When you invite someone, add, "Feel free to head home if you get tired." You'll worry less afterward. On days you want quiet, just say up front, "Today's a slow day for me."
INFP>ESTP.hidden: You can move with real energy, but you were also born good at thinking about what things mean. After a movie, don't you sometimes think hard about "What was this story really trying to say?" Share those thoughts with friends, and the talk gets even more fun.

INFP>ESFP.title: You're as happy about a friend's good news as if it were yours.
INFP>ESFP.body: When you find a great restaurant or a fun place, you tell your friends right away. When something good happens to a friend, you cheer loudly as if it happened to you. People see you as cheerful, but you also need quiet time alone.
INFP>ESFP.say: "I think you'll all love this place! Let's come together next time."
INFP>ESFP.do: When a friend recommends a song, you listen that same day and send them your thoughts.
INFP>ESFP.worry: You pack in so many fun plans that you run out of time alone. You want to keep the mood bright, so it's hard to let people see when you're sad.
INFP>ESFP.karai: Even when a friend brags about something small, you say "Amazing!" louder than they do.
INFP>ESFP.aru: Around friends you're always bright, and they say "You're so fun to be with." But on the train home, you listen to sad songs and get quietly emotional on your own.
INFP>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type who recharges by resting alone and imagines what things mean. As you gained experience, you started getting energy among people too and became able to enjoy the moment to the fullest. Lively times are truly fun for you now. The place where your heart settles is still time alone, so on the train home you listen to sad songs and quietly calm your feelings on your own.
INFP>ESFP.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and hunches or facts. Picture yourself goofing around with friends or picture yourself lost in thought alone, and your result can change.
INFP>ESFP.plus: You need quiet, emotional time because you really feel sad things too. That's why you can notice when others feel sad.
INFP>ESFP.tip: Put half a day alone between your fun plans. On a sad day, send just one close friend a message: "I'm a bit down today."
INFP>ESFP.hidden: You're great at enjoying the moment, but you were also born good at imagining what's ahead. Don't you sometimes get excited with friends about "Someday let's all do this"? Turn that talk into a real plan, and you'll be the one leading the group.
